newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call rates ease, securities yield seen down.
newsitem.headline: Indian call rates ease, securities yield seen down.

text.p: Indian call money rates opened at 7.50-8.50 percent on Friday, lower compared to the previous close of 9.00-9.50 percent, dealers said.
Call rates eased to 6.0-7.0 percent in latest quotes.
The rates are expected to touch a low of 5.0 percent as the repurchase of repo auction will inject 39.0 billion rupees into the banking system, dealers said.
Call is unlikely to ease further as the State Bank of India (SBI), a major lender, continued to to say out of the market, dealers said.
"If SBI comes in the rates may touch 3.0 percent levels today," he said. The 3-day money was quoted at 6.25-6.75 percent, dealers said.
The lower call levels and the ample inflows are expected to push down yields in the securities market, dealers said.
The prices on short-medium term securities are expected to raise by 10-15 basis points, dealers said.
The 14-day treasury bills auction is expected to attract more bidder at the around 5.0 percent levels, dealers said.
